name: Wscript.exe
description: Used by Windows to execute scripts
summary: Execute scripts stored in alternate data streams
Run scripts from scheduled tasks and Run keys for persistence
Launch PowerShell commands from a script
Run under a new name to evade detection

attack_relationships.description: Gamaredon Group has embedded malicious macros in document templates, which executed VBScript. Gamaredon Group has also delivered Microsoft Outlook VBA projects with embedded macros. Additionally, Gamaredon Group has executed VBScript files using wscript.exe.
Mustang Panda has executed a JavaScript payload utilizing wscript.exe on the endpoint.

citations.source_name: Cisco Talos MUSTANG PANDA PLUGX PUBLOAD MAY 2022

attack_relationships.description: Saint Bear has used the Windows Script Host (wscript) to execute intermediate files written to victim machines.

citations.source_name: Palo Alto Unit 42 OutSteel SaintBot February 2022

attack_relationships.description: During Operation CuckooBees, the threat actors executed an encoded VBScript file using `wscript` and wrote the decoded output to a text file.
KOCTOPUS has used VBScript to call wscript to execute a PowerShell command.

POWERSTATS has established persistence through a scheduled task using the command ”C:\Windows\system32\schtasks.exe” /Create /F /SC DAILY /ST 12:00 /TN MicrosoftEdge /TR “c:\Windows\system32\wscript.exe C:\Windows\temp\Windows.vbe”.

associated_commands.intent: Run the obfuscated VBS dropped by the COVID-19 lure's macro; it is also set in a RunOnce key so it runs again at startup.
Run the DinoTrain stager, a VBScript hidden in a .wav file name.
Run the VBScript launched from the infected USB drive's shortcut, starting the infection chain.
Run the BATELEUR JScript payload, dropped as %TEMP%\debug.txt by a spear-phishing document.
Run the VBScript launcher dropped by FIN7's malicious document.
Persistence: a scheduled task runs this every five minutes to start the QUADAGENT PowerShell payload hidden.
Persistence: a scheduled task created by Bumblebee runs this VBS every 15 minutes to load the Bumblebee DLL.
Run Shuckworm's Pterodo VBS backdoor minutes after the malicious Word document was opened.
Persistence: the OopsIE Trojan creates a scheduled task that runs itself every three minutes through a VBScript.
Run the stage 2 VBScript dropped by the malicious document's macro.
Persistence: a Run key starts this VBS at logon in Lazarus's fake interview (ClickFake) campaign.
Persistence: run a script placed in the Startup folder after the attackers' tunnelling attempts failed.
Proxy execution: abuse the signed SyncAppvPublishingServer.vbs to download and start a batch file with curl.
The Rancor DLL loader runs a command that creates a scheduled task running the dropped microsoft.vbs with wscript every 10 minutes.
The POWERSTATS backdoor keeps persistence with a scheduled task named MicrosoftEdge that runs daily at 12:00 and starts the three-step backdoor execution with wscript running Windows.vbe.
associated_commands.source_name: ClearSky MuddyWater Lebanon and Oman November 2018

associated_commands.intent: BlackByte copies itself to a remote host as obamka.js and creates a scheduled task on that host that runs the file with wscript.exe.
The Shamoon variant executes the dropped C-PDC-C-Cpy-T.vbs through WMIC to copy the malware into the Chrome folder under ProgramData.
associated_commands.source_name: Kaspersky From Shamoon to StoneDrill March 2017

associated_commands.intent: Two additional VBS scripts were observed being executed via depended.exe, the Pterodo backdoor downloaded by the first VBS file.
A scheduled task runs the dropped VBS file deep-thoughted.ppt every 10 minutes to persist across reboots.
Two additional scheduled tasks are created, this one running the VBS file tvplaylist.mov every 12 minutes, installed together with a new Pterodo variant.
After mshta launched the first command, wscript ran two VBS files that the obfuscated ~.drv created; the first contacts the command and control server.
The malicious macro finishes by running the dropped VBScript AppPool.vbs with wscript.
AppPool.vbs creates a scheduled task that runs it every minute through wscript, giving BONDUPDATER persistence.
SectopRAT created a scheduled task named Lodging for persistence that runs the script Quantifyr.js every five minutes.
associated_commands.source_name: Trend Micro Lumma Stealer GitHub Delivery January 2025

associated_commands.intent: Where the second VBS script was not dropped in the startup folder, persistence is set through Run registry keys that launch tk.vbs with wscript.exe.
The first PowerShell script returned by the C&C server registers a scheduled task named Chrome_Update that runs bot.vbe every 15 minutes.
associated_commands.source_name: ENKI Kimsuky Remote Control Tools August 2026

associated_commands.intent: The scheduled task XML runs the VBS file 11.vbs every 17 minutes, and 11.vbs then executes pp.ps1.
associated_commands.source_name: ASEC Kimsuky Malicious LNK Python Backdoor March 2026

associated_commands.intent: The command is placed in the arguments of modified browser and Outlook shortcuts so that each launch saves and runs the remote script t1.hta as %appdata%\1.vbs.
associated_commands.source_name: ASEC Kimsuky Batch File Disguised as Document Viewer June 2023

associated_commands.intent: Command line observed when the user opens the malicious VBScript attachment from WhatsApp Desktop, which starts the first stage that retrieves further VBScript components.

attack_detection_strategies.name: Behavioral Detection of Visual Basic Execution (VBS/VBA/VBScript)

analytics.description: Detects execution of VB-based scripts or macros (VBS/VBA/VBScript) through cscript.exe/wscript.exe, Office-based process chains, or HTA usage. Focuses on chained behavior: Office or HTML container spawns script host > script host spawns PowerShell, network connections, or process injection.

attack_detection_strategies.name: Cross-Platform Detection of JavaScript Execution Abuse

analytics.description: Detects JavaScript execution through WSH (wscript.exe, cscript.exe) or HTA (mshta.exe), particularly when spawned from Office macros, web browsers, or abnormal user paths. Correlates script execution with outbound network activity or system modification.

mitigations.name: Disable or Remove Feature or Program
mitigations.description: Turn off or restrict access to unneeded VB components.

mitigations.name: Execution Prevention
mitigations.description: Use application control where appropriate. VBA macros obtained from the Internet, based on the file's Mark of the Web (MOTW) attribute, may be blocked from executing in Office applications (ex: Access, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio, and Word) by default starting in Windows Version 2203.

mitigations.name: Restrict Web-Based Content
mitigations.description: Script blocking extensions can help prevent the execution of scripts and HTA files that may commonly be used during the exploitation process. For malicious code served up through ads, adblockers can help prevent that code from executing in the first place.

mitigations.name: Behavior Prevention on Endpoint
mitigations.description: On Windows 10, enable Attack Surface Reduction (ASR) rules to prevent Visual Basic scripts from executing potentially malicious downloaded content.
